name: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Carcinoma of Pancreas
aliases: Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm with Carcinoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in East Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised International Consensus Guidelines for Management of IPMN

criteria.description: Presence of enhancing mural nodules on pancreatic imaging
Main pancreatic duct dilation >10 mm or branch duct dilation >5 mm
Cytology demonstrating malignant epithelial cells in pancreatic duct fluid
New onset or worsening diabetes mellitus or pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Malignant cytology or histopathological confirmation combined with imaging evidence of ductal dilation or mural nodules
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological examination remains the gold standard for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mucin extrusion from ampulla of Vater
searchTerms: mucus leaking from bile duct opening
mucin secretion at ampulla of Vater
thick mucus discharge in digestive tract

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive jaundice due to pancreatic duct obstruction
searchTerms: yellowing skin due to bile obstruction

common.symptomName: Epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back
searchTerms: upper stomach pain radiating to back

common.symptomName: New onset or worsening diabetes mellitus

occasional.symptomName: Steatorrhea due to exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
searchTerms: fatty stools from pancreas enzyme deficiency
oily diarrhea due to poor digestion
back pain not related to posture
blood loss due to tumor in gut

laboratory: Elevated serum CA 19-9 and CEA tumor markers
Mild elevation of liver function tests (bilirubin, ALP) in obstructive jaundice
imaging: MRI/MRCP showing cystic dilation of main or branch pancreatic ducts
CT scan revealing enhancing mural nodules within cystic lesions
Endoscopic ultrasound demonstrating thickened cyst walls and mural nodules
genetic: KRAS mutations frequently detected in tumor tissue
GNAS mutations associated with IPMN progression
other: Histopathology showing papillary mucinous epithelial proliferation with cellular atypia
Cytology of pancreatic duct fluid revealing malignant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Typically solid mass without cystic dilation
No communication with pancreatic ductal system

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of pancreatic cystic lesion
Detection of enhancing mural nodules on imaging
references: Tanaka M, Fernández-del Castillo C, Adsay V, et al. International consensus guidelines 2012 for the management of IPMN and MCN of the pancreas. Pancreatology. 2012;12(3):183-197.
Kamisawa T, Wood LD, Itoi T, Takaori K. Pancreatic cancer. Lancet. 2016;388(10039):73-85.
Singhi AD, Nikiforova MN, Fasanella KE, et al. Preoperative GNAS and KRAS testing in the diagnosis of pancreatic cystic lesions. Clin Cancer Res. 2014;20(12):3292-3299.
